newsitem.title: GERMANY: German insurer Herold plans job cuts - union.
newsitem.headline: German insurer Herold plans job cuts - union.

text.p: German insurance group Deutscher Herold, a unit of German banking giant Deutsche Bank, plans to cut around one third of its in-house work-force, the banking and insurance union HBV said on Monday.
HBV said that the board of Deutscher Herold would inform the workers of the plan at an employees' meeting called at short notice.
The union said that around 900 jobs out of a total of 2,700 would go as part of a cost-cutting exercise and called for protests before the employees' meeting in Bonn.
The union said the insurance group hoped to save 100 million marks ($64.4 million) through a cost-cutting programme, ostensibly called the "Power Programme".
The plan seeks to boost productivity almost exclusively through job losses, said the chairman of Deutscher Herold's works council, Deiter Rausch.
The union said Deutscher Herold plans to cut total costs by 8.7 percent this year, while boosting premium income by six percent to 4.5 billion marks. ($ = 1.551 German Marks)
